content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I am working with a [product_name] controller ([article_no]). I have implemented a weekly timer that works correctly under normal conditions. However, during a power outage, the controller's date and time are lost, resulting in the weekly timer no longer being enabled. Please share any solutions you may have for this issue. Regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], According to the [product_name] programming software manual (weekly timer section): The internal real-time clock of [product_name] is buffered against power loss. The buffering duration depends on ambient temperature and is typically 20 days (for newer versions) or around 80 hours (for [product_name] [version_no]) at around 25°C. These devices also support battery cards or combined memory and battery modules, which extend the real-time clock buffering to several years. Hope this helps.
Hi [user_name], You can install the memory and backup battery ([article_no]) to keep the clock running during power failures.

analysis.insight_summary: Users mention that when using the [product_name] controller ([version_no]) with a weekly timer, a power outage leads to loss of date and time, causing the timer to be disabled. The device's internal battery backup lasts about 80 hours at normal temperature, and without extra battery or memory modules, the clock is not maintained during extended outages.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [product_name] controller to retain its date and time after a power loss so that the weekly timer remains functional without needing manual re-entry.
